title: Catalog-driven report requests with traffic-aware prioritization and SLA gating
creator: Priya Desai
description: Define and implement a catalog-driven intake and prioritization workflow for console/reporting requests that automatically assigns requests to delivery lanes based on observed workspace traffic patterns, cost sensitivity, and SLA entitlements. The feature should reduce ad-hoc manual triage for enterprise exports, enable predictable delivery commitments, and enforce schema/format contracts before scheduling heavy exports. This ticket covers the PM scope: intake form schema, priority scoring rules, SLA gating rules, and acceptance criteria for the engineering and design handoffs.
acceptance_criteria: A structured report request catalog (Confluence page + JSON schema) exists and is discoverable from the console support UI
Intake form maps to catalog items and populates a priority score computed from workspace traffic (tokens/day), customer tier, requested frequency, and estimated compute cost
Requests automatically routed to one of three lanes: realtime (<5s), scheduled-batch (hours), or enterprise-transfer (dedicated reserved slot), with clear SLA targets per lane
Pre-scheduling validation run to verify export schema, encryption settings, and retention policy; failing validation marks request as 'Blocked' and not scheduled
Operators can override lane assignment with an audit log and reason; overrides increment manual triage metrics
Telemetry emitted: per-request priority score, lane decision, validation result, estimated compute cost, and final fulfillment time
tasks: Draft catalog of supported report types and standard schemas (CSV, Parquet, JSONL)
Design intake UI + API contract (console + programmatic submission)
Define priority scoring function and threshold breakpoints for lanes
Implement pre-schedule validation service and failure handling
Add routing/queueing integration with scheduling service and Dedicated slot allocator
Instrument metrics and create per-lane SLA dashboards in Grafana/Console
Document runbook for manual overrides and customer communication templates
activities: 2025-08-20 - Priya Desai created ticket with initial problem statement and goals

2025-08-25 - Sync with Eng (Marco, Elena) and Design (Samira) to review catalog approach; agreed to start with 6 canonical exports: usage-summary, per-tenant-cost, token-breakdown, model-latency-rollup, workspace-audit, raw-usage-stream
2025-08-28 - PM draft of intake schema posted to Confluence (link below) for feedback; asked Eng to propose telemetry hooks for priority score
2025-09-01 - Design critique: recommend inline examples in the intake UI and progressive disclosure for enterprise options; flagged encryption/KMS settings UI as critical for adoption
2025-09-02 - Engineering triage: scoped to MVP that supports scheduled-batch and enterprise-transfer lanes; realtime lane deferred to a follow-up due to runtime constraints
review_feedback: Design: add examples and tenant-level presets to reduce form friction
Eng: need clear contract for estimated compute cost returned by estimation service; estimation should be idempotent and cached
Security: require KMS selection for exports containing PII; mark as security_review_required
Support: pre-write customer-facing templates for 'blocked for validation' and 'export scheduled' emails
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Start with a small catalog of canonical exports to limit schema permutations and speed delivery
Use traffic-aware prioritization rather than pure customer tiering to better protect latency-sensitive shared resources
Defer realtime (<5s) extraction lane to post-MVP to avoid high-throughput runtime changes
Implement pre-schedule validation strictly to reduce failed exports and repeated manual work, accepting some increase in initial triage latency
risks: Mis-estimation of compute cost could cause scheduling conflicts or unexpected spend; mitigated by conservative default multipliers
Large multi-tenant exports could impact runtime unless routed to Dedicated slots; enforce lane gating and hard caps
Schema drift from customer-provided transforms; require schema contracts and versioning in catalog
